$comment: P69 L2 (lane lm): which name a parenthesised identifier is. An ordinary identifier (object, function, parameter, enumeration constant) hides a typedef of its spelling from the end of its DECLARATOR (C 6.2.1p4, p7) — in its own initializer and in the next declarator of its declaration too; a struct/union/enum TAG never does (C 6.2.3) — not even inside its own body (check 17: `struct q1 { int a[sizeof (q1)(2)]; }` sizes by the FUNCTION q1) — nor a structure MEMBER. MEASURED 2026-10-20/21 at eb6f22a3 (pe64, images run natively), one cell per check (probes/nest k2c, k3b, k4b, k5a, k5b, g_tagcall): `int g(int); struct g {…}; (g)(2)` and `int T = 44; enum T {A = 2}; (T) - A` were REFUSED S_UnknownType, `(g)((struct g {…} *)0)` refused, `typedef int T; … int T = 44; { struct T {…}; return (T) - 2; }` RAN -2, `int T = 44, y = (T) - 2;` RAN -2 and `typedef char T; … int T = sizeof(T);` RAN 1 — the binder sketch bound a tag as an ordinary TYPE and a declarator's name only at the end of its declaration, and the analyzer's type-name lookup walked past an object to the outer typedef. gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (re-measured 2026-10-21 with check 17) build THIS file at -std=gnu2x and -std=gnu17, -O0 and -O2, and exit 42 (clang warns `_Alignof` of an expression, a GNU extension; both refuse that one check under -std=c2x -pedantic-errors). Exit 42, or the number of the first check that fails. The release arm folds the same comparisons through the optimizer.
